Featured Project
Team Project · "ABC Home Care" (Home Care Agency) · Jan–Aug 2026

Eight-Month Revenue & Reimbursement Analysis

A team analysis for a multi-payer home care agency: combining billed vs. received activity with everything the agency actually paid out — payroll plus office, marketer, and miscellaneous checks — to find the true profit, and the two open items that decide how reliable it is.

Team project

The agency's identity and payer names are withheld. All dollar figures are scaled from the original report for confidentiality — percentages and trends reflect the real findings, but the amounts are not the client's actual numbers.

Billing reports showed collections in good shape, but nobody had put collections next to the bank statement. The team pulled together payer portal and clearinghouse exports, ADP payroll files, the office check register, and bank statements, reconciled them month by month, and produced a report, Excel workbook, and slide deck for management.

How Reliable Is the Profit?

$1.66M was received from MLTC/insurance payers where no matching payroll record was found.

Reported view

  • All payments received count toward profit
  • Profit: +$1.59M (9.1%)

Matched-payroll-only view

  • Only payments with a matching payroll record count
  • Result: −$63.9K (−0.4%) — about break-even

The whole profit depends on whether those unmatched payments are truly earned — which is why confirming them was the first next step.

Key Takeaways

  • Found the true profit. Netting payroll and every cleared check against actual collections gave a 9.1% margin — and showed exactly which months lost money and why.
  • Reconciled four data sources. Payer exports, ADP payroll, the office check register, and bank statements were matched month by month in Excel.
  • Flagged what the numbers can't confirm. Unmatched payments and unlogged checks were surfaced as open items instead of being buried in the totals.
  • Turned findings into next steps. Confirm unmatched payments, classify unlogged checks, and work the $844.5K outstanding — starting with the two payers showing $0.00 in August.

ABC Home Care — Revenue Analysis

Revenue & Reimbursement Analysis — Jan–Aug 2026

Team project. Agency and payer names withheld; all dollar amounts scaled for confidentiality.

1. Executive Summary

Jan–Aug 2026: the agency billed $18,338,435.73 and received $17,493,984.67 (95.4%), leaving $844,451.06 outstanding. Total outgoing per the bank statements — ADP payroll ($13,305,236.99) plus checks for office staff, marketers and miscellaneous expenses ($2,594,647.44) — ran $15,899,884.43 (90.9% of received), for a profit of $1,594,100.24 (9.1%). July was the best month (+$571,490.69); February (−$15,318.92) and April (−$242,384.68) were losses — April ADP ran about $629,000 above a normal month.

Two items affect how reliable this profit is: (1) $1,657,984.82 was received where no matching payroll was found — if these payments are not true profit, the agency is about break-even (−$63,884.58). (2) Checks cleared per bank ($2,594,647.44) exceed checks per office records ($1,896,803.45) by $697,843.99; each unrecorded check needs to be reviewed and classified.
